label: EU(7)-PIM: pentazocine
title: Pentazocine in an older person
statement: Pentazocine is a medicine to avoid in older people because of the risk of delirium and agitation. The 2015 list suggested reducing the dose by 25% at a GFR of 10 to 50 mL/min and by 50% below 10 mL/min. These ranges use absolute GFR in mL/min. An indexed eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m² cannot be compared directly.

plain_summary: Pentazocine is an opioid-type pain medicine that can cause confusion and agitation in people aged 65 and over.

medicine_groups.name: Pentazocine
medicine_groups.note: A pentazocine supply may show the ingredient name or Fortral.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when pentazocine is supplied to a person aged 65 or over. If pentazocine is supplied and age is unknown, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is aged 65 or over. One supply is enough.
cannot_be_seen: Why it was prescribed, kidney function, and whether the person is confused or agitated.
ask_the_gp: Whether pentazocine is still needed and whether a safer pain medicine could replace it.
